notes.title: Rework of the early access achievement
notes.content:
When I started making the game I wanted to incentivize players to try it. One of the ways I decided to do that was to create an achievement rewarding people who played during early access.

I hadn't thought it through though.

As I see it, it's really important that people are able to 100% a game. Closing off an achievement to every single person who gets the game after release is a sure way to annoy a lot of people. And we can't have that of course ːsmileː

notes.title: v113 - Steam status
notes.content:
✨[b]Changes[/b]
An icon has been added that shows you if the game is properly connected to Steam's services.

If you see a red X here, the achievement will not work.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/7jxo5Eu.png[/img]

🪲[b]Bug fixes[/b]
I had packaged some wrong files with the game in v112 - the files should now be correct and the achievement should work. Again :D

notes.title: v112
notes.content:
Lots of life stuff happening these days, so activity has been scarce. I've managed to make a new build though. Here's what's new:

✨Changes
[list]
[*] New background for some screens
[/list]

🪲Bug fixes
[list]
[*] Camera movement is now steady instead of nauseating.
[*] I'm working on updating the menus and had broken the main menu. It now works again.
[*] The cartoon ended too soon.
[/list]

notes.title: Achievement working again
notes.content: I was finally able to make the achievement work again, after lots of testing. I even found a way to manually reset the achievement status so I don't have to ask others to test - so I feel pretty confident it should work now :)

notes.title: Wasps!
notes.content: I've begun implementing the wasps again (will be changed to a different creature once I figure out what). When they see you, they will stop moving and stare at you for a bit. After that they'll be so angry at you they rise up into the air and shoot at you. Unfortunately they don't see very well yet so sometimes you have to get close. And also nothing happens when you're hit. Yet. Still working on this.

notes.title: Enemy code revamp + new logo
notes.content:
I discovered a major flaw in the way enemies were coded. You probably won't notice much difference, but it need to be done :)

I also made a new logo. The existing one hadn't been changed since Ludum Dare 48. I'm not a pixel artist though, so when I eventually work with a proper graphics person something nice will be made.

notes.title: Updated intro + achievement working
notes.content:
The intro has been updated. The sounds and music were just a first draft.

The achievement is also working again. I was not aware it was broken until it was pointed out, so many thanks for that :)

notes.title: More updates to UI + new menu system on planet screen
notes.content: I've done some more tinkering with how the menus look. I've also drastically changed the menu on the planet selection screen. There are now only 2 options: "start" and "next planet". In the future I'll create a shop that has its own screen.

notes.title: Timer removed, new menu icons
notes.content:
The timer has been removed from the game.

I've also added new icons for the menu.

notes.title: New game direction + minor text fix
notes.content:
It's been a while since the last update. I've been struggling with the direction of the game. I will be removing the timer and not building the game around that concept.
The game will be put more into the control of the player in the future.

notes.title: Smooth camera
notes.content: The game now finally has smooth camera movement.

notes.title: Improvements/updates to language compatibility and post-game screen
notes.content:
Improvements to translations and the code behind language switching.

Also updated the post-game screen to accommodate the new font.

notes.title: Updates to intro and new font
notes.content:
The animation part of the intro has been finished. Huge thanks to Justin Wood - check out his work at [url=https://linestothepaper.wixsite.com/justinwoodartist]https://linestothepaper.wixsite.com/justinwoodartist[/url]. Next up for the intro is a rework of the music and sounds.

I have started implementing a new font that supports most languages. I'm still working out some kinks on this.

notes.title: Cosmetic changes
notes.content:
[list]
[*]The gem icons that appear when mining a resource now flies to the corner where the gem counter has been moved to.
[*]The timer now cycles colors more seamlessly.
[*]The particle effect for when you collect a gem is now colored depending on the type of gem.
[/list]

notes.title: Timer added + misc
notes.content:
I've added a timer on the planet screen and the levels. Time will only count when you're playing the actual game. What happens when it reaches 0? Absolutely nothing. But it cycles between colors (green -> yellowish -> red) so that's nice.

Also added some social media icons and such to the title screen.

notes.title: Planet screen rework
notes.content:
In preparation for a more detailed game loop, I've begun work on a new planet screen. The plan is that it will both become a planet selection screen and a shop where you can buy powerups. Instead of each level having a timer, your whole game session will have a timer. If you choose to move to a new planet, you will lose time but gain access to more valuable resources.

More to come on this - very far from done but for now it's functional in that you can, at least, choose which level you want to go to.

notes.title: No more taxes!
notes.content:
[list]
[*] In preparation for a rework of how time is counted in the game (to make it more in line with the story of the bank taking over Wilford's house) - taxes have now been removed. This means there's no penalty for time spent anymore.
[*] The basic red arrow on the planet screen has been replaced with Wilford's head.
[*] Planets 3 and on now work as normal too again, but they have no/few colors assigned as of yet.
[/list]

notes.title: No more pancake monsters
notes.content:
[h1]New[/h1]
[list]
[*]Every actor/object now has a discrete shadow under it.
[/list]

[h1]Changed/updated[/h1]
[list]
[*]There's now a color scheme for planet 2.
[*]Swinging the pickaxe now takes slightly longer.
[*]The salamander's have been turned into slimes (this is a temporary change).
[*]Monsters are no longer flat pancakes on the ground, but appear in the 3D world like Wilford.
[/list]

notes.title: Exit can now be found every time again
notes.content: I found a mistake in yesterday's build making the exit sometimes spawn outside the map.

notes.title: New visuals, music and fixes
notes.content:
[h1]New stuff[/h1]
[list]
[*]A particle effect has been added for when you collect a game and it hits the bottom of the screen.
[/list]

[h1]Updates[/h1]
[list]
[*]The levels now have a new palette. Not sure if I'm keeping it.
[*]New art for the gems.
[*]There's now 3D grass (wow!!!)
[*]Title music: updated
[*]Planet 2 music: completely reworked
[/list]

[h1]Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Complete rework of how the player spawned. Found a major problem with it that nobody will notice.
[*]On the score summary screen, the text for the types of gems not collected will turn red to indicate as such.
[*]When you collect a gem, the 2D icon that appears now does so in directly on top of what's been collected, rather than somewhere close.
[*]Some planets had gems spawning on top of each other.
[*]Music: it was really loud. Now it's less so.
[/list]

notes.title: Animated planets + fixes
notes.content:
[list]
[*]The planets on the level introduction screen are now animated.
[*]When Wilford is shot by a wasp, he no longer appears in the game twice afterwards.
[*]The music for the level introduction was much too loud and has been reduced.
[/list]

notes.title: Updates/fixes + new music
notes.content:
[list]
[*]New theme  track for the title screen (work in progress)
[*]The exit will now appear every time.
[*]The exit has been reworked and is now lit up by a spotlight. This allows the player to see it from a distance, even if it's behind obscured by walls.
[*]Updated the intro video with new animated segments
[*]Added features to the menu. You can now toggle between full screen and windowed mode. You can also choose to submit feedback. This will take you to a form on the Lazernaut website.
[/list]

notes.title: Intro video update
notes.content: I reworked the intro video and how it was set up internally, so it's mostly a technical change.

notes.title: Larger than normal update
notes.content:
I've been working hard on the game. As such there are some big changes in this update:

[list]
[*]Improvement in how graphics are rendered
[*]Instead of managing settings (volume etc.) on the title screen this is now done by calling up a menu. You do this by pressing Q. You can do this both on the title screen or while playing.
[*]Cosmetic changes to the title screen. Added an encouragement to sending feedback, and an explanation on the controls.
[*]Gems now breakable dirt now spawn again. They were gone with the last update due to working on the new algorithm.
[*]The timer during play now shows a clock icon instead of just "S".
[*]Probably other minor things.
[/list]

notes.title: Better randomly generated levels
notes.content:
I've implemented a new way for levels to be generated. They look much more organic now, and will become more and more complex as you progress through the game.

You can now also press Escape to exit the game.

notes.title: UI stuff
notes.content: Added a basic UI for the level screens, just to test functionality.

notes.title: Collectable gems, new music and bug fixes
notes.content:
[list]
[*] The gems can now be collected again
[*] Draft of new music for planet 1. I want the music in the first map to be more upbeat, and get more and more serious as the game progresses
[*] Fixed some bugs where too many sounds were being played at once when breaking stuff, causing lag
[/list]

notes.title: Shiny gems
notes.content:
I've adjusted the physical placement of Wilford in the physical world a little - though hardly noticeable.

I've also made it so the gems you need to pick up are very clear and shiny. They can't be picked up just yet though.

notes.title: Intro story and other small details
notes.content:
[list]
[*]First draft of an intro story is now in the game. For now it's just sketches but it will be fleshed out more in the future.
[*]Improved the particle generation when a block is broken.
[/list]

notes.title: Minor updates
notes.content:
[list]
[*] When you see the game in your library you will now see a fleshed out design of Wilford, courtesy of Justin Wood ([url=justinwoodartist.com]justinwoodartist.com[/url]).
[*] Updated the credits section
[*] Changes to the dimensions of the game level. Currently working on the way levels are generated.
[*] When you break a block containing a gem, you will see it appear and then slide to the bottom of the screen in a nice smooth way.
[/list]

notes.title: Minor update
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Changed background on some screens
[*] Improved the planet screen so you can better see where you're headed
[*] More work on the terrain generation. Optimization and coding of blocks that contain pickups.
[/list]

notes.title: Minor update
notes.content:
[list]
[*] More work on the 3D aspect of the terrain. The rocks are now 3D too. Unfortunately they're invisible. Working on that.
[*] You can now break the 3D terrain
[*] The exit is now never placed under terrain (meaning it's always visible)
[*] A sound is played if you swing the pickaxe and miss now (thanks JM Games)
[*] When you're near 3D terrain, it will become transparent so you can see what you're doing (needs tweaking)
[*] The different planned level types are now different planets. You can see them on the screen before entering a level
[/list]

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-12-23
notes.content:
- Changed the logo on startup as I've decided to put my games and music under the same banner.

- Started converting the game to include a basic 3D world. The idea was always to try and make the player a bit claustrophobic. Now that Construct 3 has added 3D functions, I'm able to get the game closer to my original vision.

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-07-08
notes.content: Just minor things today as I haven't had much time to work on Wilford this week. Testing out what not having a blank background looks like.

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-07-03
notes.content:
[list]
[*]Minor UI improvements to the leaderboard
[*]Better sound effects
[*]Better, more fluent, movement code

[/list]

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-07-01 (new player sprite)
notes.content:
[list]
[*]Completely new graphics for Wilford, including animations for when he swings his pick-axe.

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-06-30 (mostly bug fixes)
notes.content:
I've fixed a number of bugs that were annoying me. The list is as follows:

[list]
[*]The score didn't reset when starting a new game, so you could keep playing games to increase it (thanks Fripomanic)
[*]Bodies of water are now connected on all levels
[*]The exit now spawns in a place where it's visible every time
[*]Dying (getting shot 3 times by wasps) didn't transition you to the game over screen
[*]Enemies will now spawn properly every time the level starts (they used to get stuck in place after finishing 1 level
[*]Implemented new sound effects. They're likely not final.
[/list]

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-06-28
notes.content:
[list]
[*]The high score list now has a separate page on the title screen. It'll display the worldwide top 10 entries (working) and the high scores around your rank (not working).
[*]Improvement to title screen code (you could select non-existing languages before + other things)
[/list]

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-06-27
notes.content:
[list]
[*]Improved login code for the leaderboard. Now also sends the user's display name so it can be 
displayed on the leaderboard

[*]A very basic leaderboard is now displayed on the title screen

[*]Minor work on the main menu, making it a bit broken for now

[*]Changing music volume now works
[/list]

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-06-23
notes.content:
I've chosen a system called PlayFab to handle all the score keeping and leaderboards. I've started implementing it, and currently the game will submit your score. Unfortunately you can't see it, and your placement on the leaderboard. Yet.
This means that playing the game will now submit your Steam ID to Microsoft's PlayFab service, along with your score. In the future it will be possible to revoke this data from within the game, and it will also become an opt-in feature in the first place. This data will not be shared with anyone.

I've also done some work on the aesthetics, so level 1 will have patches of grass now and the rocks are now always grey. There's a lot to be done still.

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-06-19 - Achivement for cool people
notes.content: As a special thanks for playing my game during early access, you will now get an achievement after playing through 1 level. This is my thanks to all you cool people, and it will be removed once the game launches so get it now ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Update notes for 2021-06-16
notes.content:
[list]
[*]Music now plays on all levels.
[*]Enemies spawn on all levels. Also removed some unfinished path finding code that was breaking them.
[*]Changed the pre-level screen to reflect the fact that there should only be 5 levels
[*]You can now play past level 2, though subsequent levels will be a repeat but with more and tougher enemies.
[*]Fixes to the post screen - you got stuck if you didn't collect anything during the level.
[/list]
